summary: Starting with the Class of 2029, Brown became need-blind for international undergraduates — one of only a small group of US universities to do so. The Brown Promise replaces loans with scholarships in every undergraduate aid package.
covers: Need-blind admission for international applicants (from students entering in autumn 2025 onwards).
No loans: under the Brown Promise, packaged loans are replaced by scholarship funds.
eligibility: First-year applicants from any country applying to Brown's undergraduate college.
Aid is calculated from family income and assets.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application with Brown's supplement.
Choose binding Early Decision (1 November) or Regular Decision (5 January), both by 11:59 pm your local time.
Submit the CSS Profile and Brown's aid documents for international applicants.
Request a fee waiver if needed.
watch_out: Brown's Open Curriculum has no core requirements — your essays should show how you would use that freedom.
Transfer applicants may be treated differently from first-year applicants; check the international financial aid page.

faq.q: Will asking for financial aid hurt my chances?
faq.a: No. Since the Class of 2029, Brown decides on international first-year applicants without looking at whether they need aid, then meets 100% of demonstrated need. The condition is timing: apply for aid at the same time as you apply for admission.

faq.q: Do I need the SAT or ACT?
faq.a: Yes. Brown brought back its test requirement for first-year applicants from the 2024–25 cycle. It superscores the SAT and ACT and sets no minimum score.
No. All Brown aid is based on need — there are no merit awards.
